mainTopic: רב יהודה's trial before רב נחמן over calling a man a slave, public announcements of flawed lineage, and the שכינה's tie to pure families
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a tense meeting between רב יהודה and רב נחמן. רב יהודה keeps correcting רב נחמן with rulings of שמואל, and רב נחמן's wife ילתא tells him to end it. It turns out רב נחמן's court had summoned רב יהודה, and the trial begins. רב יהודה had excommunicated a man and publicly called him a slave. He defends himself with sources, including שמואל's teaching that anyone claiming to descend from the חשמונאי kings is a slave, and רב מתנה confirms that teaching. The man is declared a slave, many marriages in נהרדעא fall apart, and רב יהודה scares off an angry crowd by threatening to reveal which families are flawed. The גמרא then lists public announcements about families of flawed lineage and teaches that brazen כהנים may descend from פשחור's slaves, a view רבי אלעזר disagrees with. It ends with teachings that tie the שכינה to proper lineage and compare born Jews with converts. A new statement by רבי חמא בר חנינא begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יהודה: no sending greetings to a woman
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rejects sending greetings to ילתא even through a messenger, citing the rule that one does not ask after a woman's welfare.
steps.simpleTranslation: One does not send greetings to a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן had suggested sending greetings to his wife ילתא through a messenger. רב יהודה answers with a rule: you do not send greetings to a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues a chain in which רב יהודה keeps correcting רב נחמן's behavior with rulings of שמואל. Here even an indirect greeting through a messenger is blocked.

keyTerms.meaning: asking about someone's welfare, sending greetings

phrases.english: One does not send greetings to a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the exchange from before this section, where רב נחמן suggested sending greetings by messenger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Greetings may not be sent to a woman, even through a messenger.

steps.title: רב נחמן: send it through her husband
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן pushes back: the greeting could go through her husband, which removes any concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through her husband!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges the rule's reach. If the worry is a stranger getting close to her, let her own husband deliver the greeting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן assumes the rule is about a messenger becoming too familiar with the woman. Using the husband would remove that worry, so he thinks the greeting should be allowed.

phrases.english: Through her husband!
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is the husband here, so he is saying: send it through me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule in step 1 by offering a case that seems safe.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one does not send greetings to a woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the concern is a messenger, the husband as messenger has no such concern.

steps.title: שמואל's rule applies in every case
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that שמואל forbade greeting a woman at all, even through her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what שמואל said: One does not send greetings to a woman at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the challenge. שמואל's rule has no exceptions, not even the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כלל closes the gap רב נחמן tried to open. The rule is not only about the messenger, so changing the messenger does not help.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Shmuel said:
One does not send greetings to a woman at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening the rule: it applies in all cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban is only about a stranger acting as messenger.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל banned greeting a woman entirely, even through her husband.

steps.title: ילתא tells רב נחמן to end the exchange
steps.stepSummary: ילתא sends a message to רב נחמן telling him to finish his business with רב יהודה, so he will not keep making him look ignorant.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife sent to him: Settle his matter with him, so that he does not treat you like just another ignoramus.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן's wife ילתא steps in. She sees רב יהודה winning every exchange and tells her husband to get to the point and end it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line moves the story forward. Instead of more back-and-forth about manners, רב נחמן will now turn to why רב יהודה actually came.

keyTerms.meaning: settle his dispute, finish his business

phrases.english: His wife sent to him:
phrases.notes: This is ילתא, רב נחמן's wife.

phrases.english: Settle his dispute for him,
so that he does not make you like any other ignoramus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the etiquette exchange and sets up the shift to the real business.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ילתא urges רב נחמן to move on to the case.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks why רב יהודה came
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רב יהודה what brought him here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is the reason the Master is here?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן takes his wife's advice and asks רב יהודה why he came. This sets up the next part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the reason for the visit was never stated. This question uncovers it.

keyTerms.meaning: his reason for coming, his business
the Master, a respectful way to say 'you'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי שְׁיָאטֵיהּ דְּמָר הָכָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: What is the Master's business here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows ילתא's advice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב יהודה came to רב נחמן.

steps.title: רב יהודה: you summoned me
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that רב נחמן sent him a summons to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Master sent a summons after me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains that he came because רב נחמן's court summoned him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So רב יהודה is here as a party in a case before רב נחמן, not as a guest.

keyTerms.meaning: a summons to appear in court

phrases.english: He said to him: A summons
the Master sent after me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן's court had summoned רב יהודה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: I would never summon you
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן doubts this. He has not even learned רב יהודה's manner of speech, so how could he have summoned him?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Now, I have not even learned the Master's way of speaking, and I would send the Master a summons?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on the claim. He has just been shown up by רב יהודה, so how could he dare summon such a person?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן admits that רב יהודה is greater than him, after being corrected again and again. On that basis he finds it hard to believe he summoned him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא שׁוּתָא דְמָר לָא גְּמִירְנָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: Now, the Master's way of speaking I have not learned,
and a summons I would send to the Master?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב נחמן summoned רב יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who has not even learned רב יהודה's speech would not summon him.

steps.title: רב יהודה shows the summons
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה takes the summons out of his garment and shows it: here is the man, here is the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: He took the summons out of his bosom and showed it to him. He said to him: Here is the man and here is the document.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה proves his point by producing the actual summons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The physical document settles the doubt. 'Here is the man and here is the document' means: I am the one named, and this paper is the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: from his bosom, from inside his garment

phrases.english: He took the summons out from his bosom
and showed it to him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא גַּבְרָא וְהָא דִּסְקָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: Here is the man and here is the document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's doubt in step 7 with physical proof.
steps.raayaObject: That רב נחמן's court did summon רב יהודה.

steps.title: רב נחמן opens the case
steps.stepSummary: Since רב יהודה is already here, רב נחמן asks him to present his side, so no one says the Sages flatter each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since the Master has come here, let him state his case, so that people will not say the Sages flatter one another.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן decides to hear the case after all. This line sets up the trial that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן could have dropped the case out of respect for רב יהודה. He hears it anyway so the public will see that Torah scholars judge each other fairly and do not cover for each other.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הוֹאִיל וַאֲתָא מָר לְהָכָא
phrases.english: He said to him: Since the Master has come here,
let him state his case,
so that people will not say:
The Sages flatter one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once the summons is proven, רב נחמן moves to hear the case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is heard so it does not look like the Sages show favoritism to each other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that even a great scholar must answer in court, so justice is seen to be fair.

steps.title: Why did you excommunicate that man?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רב יהודה why he put a certain man in excommunication.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is the reason the Master excommunicated that man?
steps.whatsHappening: The trial begins. רב נחמן asks about the first thing רב יהודה did to the man: excommunicating him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man who summoned רב יהודה complained about two things. This is the first: being placed in שמתא.

keyTerms.meaning: he excommunicated him (put him in שמתא)

phrases.english: He said to him: What is the reason
the Master excommunicated that man?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא שַׁמְּתֵיהּ מָר לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First question of the trial opened in step 9.

steps.title: He mistreated an agent of the Sages
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the man caused distress to a messenger of the Sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: He caused distress to an agent of the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives his reason. The man mistreated a messenger sent by the Sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hurting a Sage's agent counts as disrespect to the Sages themselves, so it calls for a punishment.

phrases.english: He caused distress to an agent of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The man mistreated the Sages' agent.

steps.title: Then why not lashes, like רב did?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges: רב would give lashes to someone who mistreated a Sages' agent, so why not do the same?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the Master should have flogged him, since רב would flog anyone who distressed an agent of the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן questions the type of punishment. The known punishment for this offense, from רב, was lashes, not excommunication.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן accepts that the man deserved punishment. His challenge is that רב יהודה chose a different punishment from the one רב used.

phrases.english: Then let the Master flog him,
for רב would flog anyone
who caused distress to an agent of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the punishment that followed from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of excommunication as the punishment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's practice for this offense was lashes, so why excommunication?

steps.title: I gave him something stronger
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that he gave the man a harsher punishment than lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: I did to him something greater than that.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה defends his choice: excommunication is more severe than lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה is not going against רב. He holds that שמתא is a heavier punishment, so it covers lashes and more.

phrases.english: Something greater than that I did to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ranking the punishments: excommunication is more severe.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Excommunication is a departure from רב's lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Excommunication is a stronger punishment, so it is more than enough.
steps.whatToRemember: The first complaint, the excommunication, is defended: the man mistreated a Sages' agent, and שמתא is a stronger punishment than lashes.

steps.title: Why did you announce he is a slave?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks why רב יהודה publicly declared the man to be a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the Master proclaimed about him that he is a slave?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן moves to the second complaint. רב יהודה announced in public that the man was of slave lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is much more serious than a punishment. Calling someone a slave affects his whole family's status and who they may marry.

phrases.english: What is the reason the Master proclaimed about him
that he is a slave?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא אַכְרֵיז מָר עֲלֵיהּ דְּעַבְדָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second question of the trial, after the excommunication issue was settled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for publicly declaring the man a slave.

steps.title: He calls others slaves, so he is suspect
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the man keeps calling people slaves. A ברייתא teaches that whoever disqualifies others is himself flawed, and שמואל adds that he disqualifies others with his own flaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because he regularly calls people 'slaves,' and it was taught: Whoever disqualifies others is himself flawed, and he never speaks in praise of others. And שמואל said: He disqualifies others with his own flaw.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה defends the announcement with sources. Someone who keeps calling others slaves shows that he himself is a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that a person who keeps calling others unfit is a sign of his own unfit lineage. שמואל sharpens it: the exact flaw he accuses others of is his own. Since this man calls people slaves, he must be a slave.

keyTerms.meaning: used to, in the habit of

phrases.english: He said to him: Because he is in the habit of calling people "slaves,"
and it was taught: Whoever disqualifies others is himself unfit,
and he never speaks in praise of others.
And שמואל said: He disqualifies with his own flaw.
phrases.notes: In other words, the flaw he keeps blaming on others is really his own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The man's habit of calling others slaves shows he is a slave, based on a ברייתא and שמואל.

steps.title: Suspicion is not grounds for an announcement
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges: שמואל only meant that we should suspect such a person. Did he say we may publicly announce it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that שמואל said this to suspect him. Did he say it to announce it about him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks how far רב יהודה took the source. שמואל's rule gives grounds for suspicion, not for a public declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a big difference between privately suspecting someone and publicly labeling him a slave. רב נחמן argues that שמואל's statement only supports the first, so רב יהודה went too far.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not rejecting שמואל's rule. He accepts it but limits it: it allows suspicion, not a public announcement.

phrases.english: Granted that שמואל said it so that we should suspect him;
but to proclaim it about him, did he say that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how רב יהודה used the source in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's use of שמואל's statement to justify a public announcement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's rule only supports suspicion, which is much weaker than a public declaration that someone is a slave.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the bar for the rest of the trial: רב יהודה will need a stronger basis to justify the public announcement.

steps.title: The man protests that he comes from royal stock
steps.stepSummary: The litigant arrives and objects to רב יהודה: how can you call me a slave when I come from the חשמונאי kings?
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, that litigant arrived from נהרדעא. He said to רב יהודה: You call me a slave? I come from the house of the חשמונאי kings!
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The man who was called an עבד shows up and angrily objects that his family is royal, not slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now רב נחמן was questioning רב יהודה. Now the man himself pushes back with a family claim. That claim sets up רב יהודה's answer, which uses the very same claim against him.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile, while this was going on
The litigant, the person in the court case

phrases.english: Meanwhile
that litigant came from נהרדעא.
phrases.notes: These words are in round brackets, so some versions of the text leave them out.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא בַּר דִּינֵיהּ לְרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: That litigant said to רב יהודה:
Me you call a "slave",
I, who come from the house of the חשמונאי kings?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story behind רב נחמן's challenge. The man himself now objects.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's public declaration that the man is a slave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man from royal lineage cannot be a slave.

steps.title: רב יהודה quotes שמואל about the חשמונאי claim
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that שמואל taught that anyone claiming to come from the חשמונאי family is a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to him: This is what שמואל said: Anyone who says 'I come from the house of חשמונאי' is a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה turns the man's own claim against him. Saying you come from the חשמונאי family is itself a sign that you are a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This also answers רב נחמן's challenge in step 16. רב יהודה is no longer relying only on a general suspicion. He has a specific teaching from שמואל that makes this claim a clear marker of slave status.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what שמואל said:
Anyone who says, "I come from the house of חשמונאי"
is a slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the man's protest, and also gives a firm basis against רב נחמן's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a specific teaching that turns the man's claim into evidence against him.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Royal lineage means the man cannot be a slave.
steps.terutzMaskana: The claim of חשמונאי lineage itself shows that he is a slave.

steps.title: רב נחמן: a ruling quoted after the fact is not believed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן cites רב: a חכם who reports a הלכה only after a case involving him has come up is not listened to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Doesn't the Master agree with what רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא in the name of רב? Any Torah scholar who comes to teach a הלכה is listened to if he said it before the case happened. If not, he is not listened to.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks the timing of רב יהודה's quote. רב יהודה is only bringing up שמואל's teaching now, in the middle of his own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule says that a חכם who is involved in a case might be biased. So a teaching he quotes only after the case comes up is not accepted. רב נחמן claims that רב יהודה's report of שמואל should therefore be ignored.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah scholar who comes to teach a הלכה
We listen to him, his ruling is accepted

steps.whyThisMatters: This is an important rule about trusting a חכם's testimony about a הלכה. It is believed fully only if he said it before he was personally involved.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Does the Master not hold
this, which רבי אבא said
that רב הונא said that רב said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁמּוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה וּבָא,
phrases.english: Any Torah scholar who comes to teach a הלכה,

phrases.aramaic: אִם קוֹדֶם מַעֲשֶׂה אֲמָרָהּ – שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ,
phrases.english: if he said it before the incident, we listen to him,
and if not, we do not listen to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רב יהודה's quote of שמואל in step 18 can be trusted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reliability of רב יהודה's report of שמואל's teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה cited the teaching only after he was involved in the case, so by רב's rule it is not accepted.

steps.title: רב יהודה: רב מתנה can back me up
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that רב מתנה also heard שמואל's teaching and supports him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to him: There is רב מתנה, who stands with me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers by pointing to a second witness. רב מתנה is not involved in the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule only worries about a biased scholar. If another scholar with no involvement heard the same teaching, the concern goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Who stands with me, who agrees with my report

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא אִיכָּא רַב מַתְנָה
phrases.english: He said to him: Here, there is רב מתנה,
who stands with me.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִיכָּא רַב מַתְנָה דְּקָאֵי כְּווֹתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge about timing by bringing an independent witness.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Independent support from a witness with no involvement in the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's report stands alone and is suspect.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב מתנה, who is not involved, can confirm the teaching.

steps.title: רב מתנה arrives and רב יהודה asks him
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה, who had not been in נהרדעא for thirteen years, arrives that very day. רב יהודה asks whether he remembers what שמואל said at the ferry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה had not seen נהרדעא for thirteen years. That very day he came. רב יהודה said to him: Does the Master remember what שמואל said when he was standing with one foot on the riverbank and one foot on the ferry?
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows that רב מתנה arrived at just the right moment. This sets up the test of whether he will confirm the teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה does not say the teaching himself. He only reminds רב מתנה of the setting, so רב מתנה's answer is truly his own memory. The detail about the riverbank shows that both heard it at one specific moment.

phrases.english: רב מתנה had not seen נהרדעא
for thirteen years.
That day he came.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּכִיר מָר מַאי אֲמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
phrases.english: He said to him: Does the Master remember what שמואל said
when he was standing with one foot on the riverbank
and one foot on the ferry?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts step 20's answer into action by calling on the witness.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב מתנה remembers שמואל's statement from that occasion

steps.title: רב מתנה confirms שמואל's words and the reason
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה repeats שמואל's teaching and explains it. The only true חשמונאי survivor was a girl who announced from a roof that anyone claiming that lineage is a slave, and then she fell and died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: This is what שמואל said: Anyone who says 'I come from the house of the חשמונאי kings' is a slave. None of them remained except that young girl who went up to the roof, raised her voice and said: Anyone who says 'I am from the house of חשמונאי' is a slave. She fell from the roof and died.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה confirms exactly what רב יהודה reported. He also adds the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the teaching has an independent second witness, so רב נחמן's objection is answered. The reason is that the real חשמונאי line ended with this girl. So anyone claiming that descent must come from the slaves of that household.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two speakers. רב מתנה is quoting שמואל, and שמואל is quoting the girl. The words 'anyone who says...is a slave' appear twice: first as שמואל's ruling, then as the girl's original announcement.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what שמואל said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל דְּאָמַר מִדְּבֵית חַשְׁמוֹנַאי מַלְכָּא קָאָתֵינָא –
phrases.english: Anyone who says, "I come from the house of the חשמונאי kings"
is a slave,
since none remained of them
except that young girl who went up to the roof
and raised her voice and said:
Anyone who says, "I am from the house of חשמונאי"
is a slave.
She fell from the roof and died.
phrases.notes: With her gone, no true member of the family was left, so only the slaves of that household remained.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל כֹּל דְּאָמַר מִדְּבֵית חַשְׁמוֹנַאי מַלְכָּא קָאָתֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's question by confirming the teaching word for word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. שמואל said that anyone claiming חשמונאי descent is a slave, because the only true survivor was the girl who announced this and then died.

steps.title: The man is publicly declared a slave
steps.stepSummary: After the confirmation, they publicly announced that the man is a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: They announced about him that he is a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. Since the teaching was confirmed, the public announcement against the man stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's objections are fully answered. The teaching came from two witnesses and gives a specific basis, not just a suspicion. So the man's slave status is announced.
steps.whatToRemember: A חכם's report of a הלכה given in the middle of his own case needs independent support. Here רב מתנה supplied it. The claim to come from the חשמונאי family was treated as a sign of slave status.

phrases.english: They announced about him that he is a slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical result from רב מתנה's confirmation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: With שמואל's teaching confirmed by an independent witness, the man was publicly declared a slave.

steps.title: Marriages Undone and an Angry Crowd
steps.stepSummary: After the announcement, many כתובות in נהרדעא were torn up, and people chased רב יהודה to stone him.
steps.simpleTranslation: That day several marriage contracts were torn up in נהרדעא. When רב יהודה was leaving, people went after him to stone him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the announcement in step 23 caused many marriages in נהרדעא to fall apart. Angry people chased רב יהודה, which sets up his response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once one man was exposed as a slave, other families tied to him were exposed too, so their marriages were no good. The people blamed רב יהודה for revealing it.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא יוֹמָא אִקַּרְעָן כַּמָּה כְּתוּבָּתָא בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא.
phrases.english: That day, several marriage contracts were torn up in Nehardea.
phrases.notes: People found out they had married into slave families, so those marriages were undone.

phrases.english: When he was leaving,
phrases.notes: "He" is רב יהודה.

phrases.english: they went out after him to stone him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יוֹמָא אִקַּרְעָן כַּמָּה כְּתוּבָּתָא בִּנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what happened as a result of the public announcement in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Exposing the slave's lineage caused many marriages in נהרדעא to be undone, and the crowd turned on רב יהודה.

steps.title: רב יהודה Silences the Crowd
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה threatens to reveal שמואל's teaching about the 'dove' and 'raven' families, and the crowd drops its stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told them: If you keep quiet, fine. If not, I will reveal what שמואל said: there are two families in נהרדעא, one called the house of the dove and one called the house of the raven. Remember: the impure bird means impure, the pure bird means pure. They dropped their stones, and the stones piled up into a dam in the נהר מלכא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the angry crowd with a threat. If they keep attacking, he will reveal exactly which families are flawed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל had a code: the 'raven' family, named after an impure bird, has flawed lineage, and the 'dove' family, named after a pure bird, is fine. The attackers were afraid of being exposed, so they gave up. So many stones were dropped that they blocked the river.

phrases.english: He said to them:
If you are quiet, be quiet;
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the word in square brackets.

phrases.english: and if not, I will reveal about you
this that Shmuel said:
There are two families in Nehardea:
one is called "the dove's house,"
and one is called "the raven's house."
And your sign: impure is impure, pure is pure.
phrases.notes: The raven is a non-kosher bird, so that family is flawed. The dove is kosher, so that family is fine.

phrases.english: They threw those stones from their hands,
and a dam formed in the Malka River.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יהודה's response to the crowd chasing him in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A threat to reveal שמואל's code for the flawed families, which makes the crowd back off.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole נהרדעא story shows how seriously lineage was guarded, and how much people feared being exposed.

steps.title: רב יהודה's Announcements in פומבדיתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה publicly names certain people in פומבדיתא as slaves or a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה announced in פומבדיתא: אדא and יונתן are slaves. יהודה בר פפא is a ממזר. בטי בר טוביה was too proud to accept a גט שחרור, so he is still a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts a list of public announcements about people with flawed lineage. Here רב יהודה names specific people in his city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These announcements warned the public not to marry these people. בטי בר טוביה could have become free, but he refused the document, so he stayed a slave.

keyTerms.meaning: A document of freedom for a slave (גט שחרור)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda proclaimed in Pumbedita:
Adda and Yonatan are slaves.
Yehuda bar Pappa is a mamzer.
Bati bar Tuviyya, out of arrogance,
did not accept a bill of freedom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the נהרדעא story to a list of other public announcements about flawed lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אדא and יונתן are slaves, יהודה בר פפא is a ממזר, and בטי בר טוביה is still a slave.

steps.title: רבא's Announcement in מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא declares five families in מחוזא to be of flawed lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא announced in מחוזא: the families בלאי, דנאי, טלאי, מלאי and זגאי are all flawed.
steps.whatsHappening: The list continues with another public announcement, this time by רבא in his city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a whole family name, not just one person, is marked as flawed, so anyone from these families may not marry into a family with proper lineage.

phrases.english: Rava proclaimed in Mechoza:
Balla'ai, Danna'ai, Talla'ai,
phrases.notes: These are family names.

phrases.english: Malla'ai, Zagga'ai: all of them are flawed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second announcement, parallel to רב יהודה's in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five named families in מחוזא are of flawed lineage.

steps.title: Families Who Are Really גבעונים
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה identifies two groups as descendants of the גבעונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: the גובאי are really גבעונים. The דורנוניתא are from the village of the נתינים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains that certain group names are hidden forms of גבעונים, who are not allowed to marry into Israel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier announcements about slaves and ממזרים, this identifies groups as גבעונים, also called נתינים. Their names had changed over time, so people might not realize who they were.

keyTerms.meaning: נתינים, another name for the descendants of the גבעונים

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Gova'ai are Gibeonites,
Dorenunita is the village of the Netinim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of flawed groups, now naming groups descended from the גבעונים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גובאי and the people of דורנוניתא are גבעונים.

steps.title: בי כובי Are All Slaves
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says everyone in בי כובי of פומבדיתא descends from slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: the people of בי כובי in פומבדיתא are all descended from slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: One more item on the list: רב יוסף marks a whole neighborhood as descended from slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This widens the scope from families to an entire place. Everyone living there is assumed to be of slave lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: Bei Kuvei, a place in פומבדיתא

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
This Bei Kuvei of Pumbedita:
all of them are from slaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הַאי בֵּי כוּבֵּי דְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last item in the list of announcements about flawed lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All residents of בי כובי in פומבדיתא are descendants of slaves.

steps.title: פשחור's Slaves Mixed Into the כהונה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that the many slaves of פשחור בן אמר blended into the כהונה, and brazen כהנים come from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: פשחור בן אמר had four hundred slaves, and some say four thousand, and all of them blended into the כהונה. Any כהן who is brazen comes only from them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching: the slaves of a well-known כהן became mixed in with real כהנים. שמואל gives a sign for spotting their descendants: brazenness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since these slaves belonged to a כהן, people assumed they were כהנים too. שמואל teaches that a rude, brazen character shows that a 'כהן' really comes from those slaves.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן in the days of ירמיהו

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Four hundred slaves,
and some say four thousand slaves,
belonged to Pashchur ben Immer,
phrases.notes: He was a כהן in the days of ירמיהו (ירמיהו 20:1).

phrases.english: and all of them blended into the priesthood.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל כֹּהֵן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ עַזּוּת פָּנִים
phrases.english: And any priest who has brazenness
is only from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת עֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of hidden slave lineage, now inside the כהונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פשחור's slaves blended into the כהונה, and brazen כהנים descend from them.

steps.title: אביי: They Sit in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that these descendants all sit in the rows of נהרדעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: all of them sit in the rows of נהרדעא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a comment to שמואל's teaching, saying where these descendants are found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי points out that the descendants of פשחור's slaves are among the respected people of נהרדעא. So even people sitting in honored places may have this hidden flaw.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They all sit in the rows that are in Nehardea.
phrases.notes: He means the rows of honored seats there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כּוּלְּהוּ יָתְבָן בְּשׁוּרָא דְבִנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to שמואל's teaching in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The descendants of פשחור's slaves sit in the honored rows of נהרדעא.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: Don't Suspect a Brazen כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי אלעזר disagrees: a brazen כהן should not be suspected, since כהנים are known to be quarrelsome.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי אלעזר, who said: If you see a brazen כהן, do not suspect him, as the פסוק says: 'Your people are like those who quarrel with a כהן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that שמואל's teaching from step 30 is argued on by רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said brazenness is a sign of slave lineage. רבי אלעזר says brazenness is normal for real כהנים, as the פסוק shows people quarreling with a כהן, so it proves nothing about lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who quarrel with a כהן

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Elazar,
for Rabbi Elazar said:
If you see a priest who is brazen,
do not suspect him,
phrases.notes: Meaning, don't suspect that his lineage is flawed.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "For your people are like those who quarrel with a priest."
phrases.notes: הושע 4:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opinion that disagrees with שמואל's sign of brazenness in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, a brazen כהן should not be suspected of flawed lineage.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not refuting שמואל here. It is only noting that רבי אלעזר holds a different view.

steps.title: The שכינה Does Not Testify for an Improper Marriage
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that when the שכינה rests on Israel, it testifies for the tribes but not for someone who married a woman unfit for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין בר רב אדא said in the name of רב: Anyone who marries a woman who is not fit for him: when הקדוש ברוך הוא rests His שכינה, He testifies about all the tribes but not about him. As it says: 'The tribes of God, a testimony for Israel.' When is it a testimony for Israel? When the tribes are truly tribes of God.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching about the spiritual cost of marrying improperly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the tribes being 'tribes of God' with their being a 'testimony.' רב reads this as a condition: God testifies only for families with proper lineage, so someone who marries improperly loses that testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Not fit or proper for him to marry

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin bar Rav Adda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַנּוֹשֵׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁאֵינָהּ הוֹגֶנֶת לוֹ,
phrases.english: Anyone who marries a woman who is not fit for him,
when the Holy One, Blessed be He, rests His Divine Presence,
He testifies about all the tribes
but does not testify about him,
as it is stated: "The tribes of the Lord, a testimony to Israel."
phrases.notes: תהלים 122:4

phrases.english: When is it a testimony to Israel?
When the tribes are the tribes of the Lord.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from lists of flawed families to the spiritual consequence of marrying improperly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's testimony through the שכינה covers only families whose lineage is proper.
steps.whatToRemember: Proper lineage is not only a legal matter. רב teaches that God's own testimony for Israel depends on the tribes staying 'tribes of God.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the earlier announcements and the נהרדעא story treat lineage so seriously: it affects the שכינה's connection to each family.

steps.title: The Divine Presence rests only on families of pure lineage
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא teaches that the שכינה rests only on משפחות מיוחסות. He proves it from a פסוק that says 'all the families of Israel' and not 'all Israel.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says: When ה׳ rests His Presence, He rests it only on families of pure lineage in Israel. The proof is the פסוק: 'At that time, says ה׳, I will be God to all the families of Israel.' It does not say 'to all Israel.' It says 'to all the families.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives another statement connecting the שכינה to pure family lineage. He brings a פסוק as his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on one extra word. The פסוק could have said 'all Israel,' but it says 'all the families of Israel.' He reads 'families' as the well-known families with clean lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is stated (introduces a פסוק)
It does not say X, but rather Y (points to a precise word choice)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina says:
When the Holy One, Blessed be He, rests His Divine Presence,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁרֶה אֶלָּא עַל מִשְׁפָּחוֹת מְיוּחָסוֹת שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: He rests it only on families of pure lineage in Israel,
as it is stated:
"At that time, says the Lord,
I will be God to all the families of Israel,"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 30:25

phrases.english: "To all Israel" is not stated,
but rather "to all the families."
phrases.notes: He reads 'families' as the known families with clean lineage, not every single Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's theme from step 33 that the שכינה is tied to proper lineage. Here a פסוק is brought as the source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שכינה rests only on families of pure lineage, as the פסוק says 'all the families of Israel' and not 'all Israel.'

steps.title: Born Jews have an advantage over converts
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא compares two פסוקים. For born Jews, ה׳ says 'I will be their God' first. For גרים, 'you shall be My people' comes first. This shows an extra advantage for born Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they shall be My people.' רבה בר רב הונא says: This shows an extra advantage that born Jews have over converts. About born Jews it says: 'I will be their God, and they shall be My people.' About converts it says: 'Who is he that pledged his heart to come close to Me, says ה׳? You shall be My people, and I will be your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the words 'they shall be My people' and brings רבה בר רב הונא, who compares how two פסוקים are worded for born Jews and for converts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is the order of the two halves. For born Jews, ה׳ first declares 'I will be their God.' He reaches out to them first. For converts, the convert must first pledge his heart and become 'My people,' and only then does ה׳ say 'I will be your God.'

keyTerms.meaning: An extra advantage or higher level
Whereas here... but there (sets up a contrast)

steps.confusionAlert: Both פסוקים contain the same two phrases. The whole lesson comes only from which phrase comes first.

phrases.english: "[And they] shall be My people,"
phrases.notes: These words finish the פסוק quoted in step 34. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna says:
This is an extra advantage
that exists between born Jews and converts.
For regarding born Jews, it is written about them:
"And I will be their God,
and they shall be My people,"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 37:27

phrases.english: whereas regarding converts it is written:
"Who is he that has pledged his heart
to come close to Me, says the Lord?
And you shall be My people,
and I will be your God."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 30:21–22. Notice the order is flipped compared to the first פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: זוֹ מַעֲלָה יְתֵירָה יֵשׁ בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the same section of ירמיהו quoted in step 34. It moves from lineage within Israel to the difference between born Jews and converts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Born Jews have an extra advantage. ה׳ draws close to them first, while converts must first draw close to Him.

steps.title: Converts are as difficult for Israel as a scab
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו says גרים are hard for Israel like a ספחת. He learns this from the shared root in 'ונספחו' (said about converts) and 'ספחת' (a type of צרעת).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו says: Converts are as hard for Israel as a scab. The פסוק says: 'The convert will join them, and they will attach (ונספחו) to the house of יעקב.' Here it says 'ונספחו,' and elsewhere it says 'for a swelling and for a scab (ספחת).'
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds a statement about converts. He proves it by matching a word in a פסוק about converts with a similar word about a skin affliction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a word link. 'ונספחו' (they will attach) and 'ספחת' (a scab) share the same root. That connection lets רבי חלבו compare converts joining Israel to a ספחת on the skin.

keyTerms.meaning: A scab, a skin affliction listed among types of צרעת
It is written here... and it is written there (links two פסוקים by a shared word)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo says:
Converts are as hard for Israel as a scab,
as it is stated:
"And the convert shall join them,
and they shall attach themselves to the house of Jacob."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 14:1

phrases.english: Here it is written "and they shall attach (venispechu),"
and there it is written "for a swelling and for a scab."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:56. Both words share the same root, and that link is the proof.
